title: Phase A — Canonical Agent Registry
description: Register the EQCOFE Agent Layer Phase A operational specialization registry for A0 through A10 without changing or weakening Multi-Agent V1.6 authority, review, verification, security, human-gate, scope, lock, risk or merge semantics.

why_low: The task is documentation-only and writes only the new Agent Layer registry, its own Task Contract, and the generated Task Catalog.
No Project Map HIGH sensitive zone is touched.
No controller, workflow, protection, product runtime, API, database, migration, pricing, inventory, auth, payment or financial behavior is changed.
The registry explicitly preserves the existing V1.6 authority model rather than redefining it.
risk_rationale.escalation_condition: If deterministic classification or provider state raises risk above LOW, stop and follow the higher-risk policy; no downgrade is permitted.

dependencies.name: Canonical V1.6 governance and authority model

external_gate_evidence.rule: LOW-risk Agent Registry task requires exact-artifact ACTIVE LOCK plus deterministic verification; Review/Security/Human gates are not independently required unless deterministic risk escalates.

acceptance_criteria.description: PHASE-A-AGENT-REGISTRY.md defines exactly A0 through A10 with the approved canonical role names and high-level responsibilities.
The registry states that the Agent Layer is operational specialization only and does not replace or weaken V1.6 governance or authority separation.
The common output contract includes CLAIMED_CANONICAL_PASS = NO and agent outputs are explicitly non-canonical for Review, Verification and Security Gate authority.
Deterministic classification remains LOW with Human Gate NOT REQUIRED; any higher deterministic result blocks LOW execution and requires higher-risk policy.
Task Catalog is generated consistently from Task Contracts and docs automation check passes.
The PR changes exactly the three authorized write-scope files and no forbidden path.
Exact-head required Canonical CI, Phase A and Merge Policy checks pass for the exact artifact.
The task reaches canonical completion only through protected Merge Policy transport followed by exact-SHA post-merge verification and terminal Lock release.
